question.text: The difference between a bank and an NBFC includes:

answer.text: NBFCs can accept demand deposits while banks cannot
NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits and do not have the facility of issuing cheques
NBFCs have deposit insurance while banks do not
There is no significant difference between banks and NBFCs

explanation.text: The Logic: NBFCs differ from banks in three workbook-stated ways: NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits, do not have the facility of issuing cheques drawn on themselves, and DICGC deposit insurance is not available to NBFC depositors. Banks have all three of these capabilities and protections. The Trap: Candidates may swap which entity can accept demand deposits or which one has deposit insurance. The source-stated position is the opposite of options A and C — banks accept demand deposits and have DICGC cover, NBFCs do not. Note: Source basis is p.95 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025).
